items.stem: A firm designates a principal to approve retail communications. Under FINRA's communications framework, which category generally requires principal approval BEFORE first use?

options.text: Retail communication distributed to more than 25 retail investors within any 30-day period
options.rationale: Correct: retail communications to more than 25 retail investors in 30 days generally require principal approval before first use.

options.text: A one-to-one email to a single existing customer
options.rationale: A single personalised email is correspondence, reviewed under correspondence procedures rather than pre-use principal approval.

options.text: An internal memo to registered representatives
options.rationale: Internal communications are not communications with the public.

options.text: An oral statement made on a phone call
options.rationale: Oral statements are not written or electronic communications subject to the pre-use approval rule.

items.explanation: Correct: retail communications to more than 25 retail investors in 30 days generally require principal approval before first use.

items.stem: A branch manager wants to reduce how often transactions are reviewed to save time. As principal, what is the governing consideration for setting review frequency in the firm's written supervisory procedures?

options.text: The firm's size, business mix and risk, so reviews are reasonably designed to achieve compliance
options.rationale: Correct: WSPs must be reasonably designed for the firm's business and risk; frequency is risk-based, not arbitrary.
Convenience is not a permissible basis for supervisory review frequency.

options.text: A fixed annual review for all activity regardless of risk
options.rationale: A single fixed interval ignores the risk-based design standard.

options.text: Only reviews triggered by a customer complaint
options.rationale: Supervision must be proactive, not solely complaint-driven.

items.explanation: Correct: WSPs must be reasonably designed for the firm's business and risk; frequency is risk-based, not arbitrary.

items.stem: A principal reviews a new municipal-securities underwriting the firm is joining. Which TWO oversight points fall squarely within the principal's supervisory responsibility here? (Select TWO)

options.text: Confirming communications about the new issue meet content and approval standards
options.rationale: Correct: review of offering communications is a principal supervisory duty.

options.text: Checking the allocation against free-riding and withholding restrictions
options.rationale: Correct: policing allocation of a hot issue is within supervisory responsibility.

options.text: Personally setting the coupon rate offered to issuers
options.rationale: Pricing negotiation is a business function, not the principal's supervisory review duty.

options.text: Guaranteeing the bonds will not decline in value
options.rationale: No one can guarantee market value; this is not a supervisory obligation.

options.text: Selecting which retail customer receives the largest social-media following
options.rationale: This is irrelevant to supervisory duties over an underwriting.

items.explanation: Correct: review of offering communications is a principal supervisory duty. Correct: policing allocation of a hot issue is within supervisory responsibility.
